text:
maria: Quick heads-up — FP8 calibration sweep we ran on branch quant/fp8-corpus2 shows a perf regression on long-context workloads when we include multi-document legal texts in the calib set.

lucas: What numbers are you seeing? end-to-end or kernel-level?

maria: Kernel-level first: on A100s, fp8 GEMM kernels for layernorm-ish op show ~12% slower median (measured with perf-ci microbench) when corpus includes docs > 8k tokens. End-to-end p99 latency up ~9% on long-context chat tests. :eyes: 

zhao: That's surprising — calib should only affect quant scales not kernel path. Could this be KV cache warmup differences? Longer sequences change kv cache reuse pattern.

anya: Did we accidentally include padding-heavy examples that trigger different batching heuristics?

maria: I thought of that. Sampled the calib set: ~18% of examples are concatenated emails (lots of short segments but long total length). Hard to tell if per-channel vs per-tensor calib amplifies this.

lucas: Maybe per-channel calibration produced outlier scales that pick a slower FP8 kernel (fallback) or disabled some fused kernels. Do we have kernel selection logs from the runtime?

bench-bot: deploy-bench: finished microbench set 'fp8-kernel-smoke' — artifacts at https://ci.internal/runs/4521 :white_check_mark:

zhao: I pulled the artifacts: kernel selector shows we switched from 'fused-gemm-v2' to 'fallback-gemm' for 12 layers when using that corpus.

maria: ok that's the link — looks like per-channel calib widened scale variance for certain weights; runtime's kernel-chooser prefers numeric stability path with extra casts.

anya: Two follow-ups: 1) can we try per-tensor calibration only 2) generate a "trimmed" calib corpus that excludes multi-doc concatenations and compare.

lucas: I can run a quick A/B. Proposed plan: create three calibs: (A) per-channel full corpus, (B) per-tensor full corpus, (C) per-channel trimmed (no concatenated-docs). Run kernel selector trace + perf microbench and end-to-end chat SLO tests.

maria: +1. Also add KV-warmup trace, and include batching simulation with prefix caching enabled. Use these configs:
```json
{ "batching": { "max_batch": 64, "prefer_latency": false }, "kv_prefetch": true }
```

lucas: I'll queue jobs today. Expect initial artifacts in ~3h. If per-tensor avoids the fallback kernel we may prefer that for Dedicated and Redwood Private by default. But need quality check: per-tensor can degrade output sometimes.

zhao: Right — add eval pass against our cal-val set (200 prompts) and diff logits to catch regressions.

anya: Also log a quick doc about corpus hygiene: mark concatenated-docs as a sampling bucket 'concat' so they can be optionally excluded from calib. :memo:

maria: Agree. I'll open a short PR to add 'concat' tagger to the sampler and push trimmed sets to s3:/redwood/quant/calib_trimmed/2623456789.

lucas: nice. Tag me on the PR. Everyone, if you see odd kernel flip in perf traces, paste the small kernel-selector snippet (layer idx + chosen kernel) into the thread so we can correlate.

zhao: Will do. bench-bot: please re-run 'fp8-kernel-smoke' with KB=1 and KB=8 (kv warmup sizes) — helps isolate cache interaction.

bench-bot: queued 'fp8-kernel-smoke' (kb=1,8) — run id 4522

maria: Thanks. If this ends up being a corpus artifact we should add a warning in Optimize: 'avoid concatenated multi-doc examples in calibration sets unless using explicit kv-warmup profiling'

anya: Good idea. Keeps customers from accidental perf hits.

lucas: I'll update the internal runbook after results. End.
